# Motivation

## Nature is invisible in the accounts

- Ecosystems supply services the economy depends on, from pollination and soil retention to coastal protection and carbon storage, yet none of them appear in standard national accounts.
- What is not measured goes unmanaged: the loss of these services surfaces only later, as lower yields, higher damages and higher prices.
- The Gross Ecosystem Product (GEP) account values what ecosystems supply, country by country and service by service, so natural capital can be tracked alongside GDP.
- The same service models also drive scenario analysis: how climate and land-use scenarios change the services economies depend on, feeding the NGFS and GTAP pipelines.

## Why one reviewed library

- Each GEP service model was developed by a different contributor in a different repository, with its own layout, path conventions and aggregation habits.
- Numbers from that landscape are hard to trust. The survey found hardcoded personal paths, modules cloned from other services without respecification, silent country joins and reports that could not be reproduced.
- One home with one template makes every service runnable by anyone, verifiable by rerun, and consumable by both the GEP account and the economic models.
- The discipline this enables has already corrected headline numbers, including one claim of our own.

# What global_invest is

## One module, two outputs per service

- The library holds one folder per ecosystem service, all on the same file convention.
- Each service exposes two outputs from the same science: a GEP valuation per country, and an NGFS scenario shock for the GTAP pipeline.
- Writing the science once and exposing it two ways keeps the valuation and the shock from drifting apart.
- The library carries no consumer scenario names. Consumers inject their naming through scenario maps and required configuration.

## The template every service follows

- Five files per service: thin runners, tasks, science functions, initialize, and a method document that renders from the code.
- One runner per task tree, with no mode switches inside a runner.
- initialize_paths is the single source of truth for inputs, resolved as reference paths so the same code runs on any machine.
- Aggregation is on r250, one row per country. The r264 crosswalk is used only for maps.
- Every number is verified by running the model, never by trusting a report.

| fisheries | shock only | valuation external (CWoN) |

## Verification discipline, and what it caught

- Run first, conform second, and verify every conform step against the cached run. An additive gate audits each branch against develop.
- Write-time invariants check every shock table before it is written, and a canonical-row rule guards every country aggregation.
- Caught so far: a 23.5 percent double-count in the carbon GEP, a two-spelling baseline bug, and a stale-input trap in the erosion chaining.
- It also caught one claim of our own: the coastal report's numbers are the EEZ-only aggregation by design, matched exactly by our run.

# Open questions

## Open decisions for the room

- The coastal shoreline convention: EEZ-only at $22.84bn or all rows at $102.18bn with a terrestrial mask.
- The pollination definition: raster-side $18.28B or FAO-side $515B, identical ranking.
- The map convention (r264 vs dissolved r250), crop units labeling, and the base year (2019 vs 2023).
- Universe structure: one module per service or per subgroup, and whether subsistence subgroups are in scope.

## Questions for service owners

- coastal_protection: which state produced the in-code $73.0bn against the verified $36.72bn.
- extractive_materials: the written source of the 0.49 factor.
- livestock_provision: the item list has no milk, crop's coefficients are reused, the country join loses countries.
- coastal_carbon: the EEZ-only rationale and the report's marsh and seagrass input versions.
- erosion and landslide: the submission inputs and a machine-readable reference.
- renewable_energy: whether the code or the drive reference CSVs are blessed.

# Roadmap

## The target universe

- The service coordination sheet lists roughly 26 services. The library currently covers ten.
- The sheet splits renewable energy into wind, solar and geothermal, where the library has one module.
- Crop, livestock and fisheries carry subsistence subgroups beyond the current commercial scope.
- Extractive energy (oil, gas and coal) is distinct from extractive materials and not yet built.

## Next steps

- Tuesday: the four-PR round, with global_invest and ngfs_pnas reviewed as one mutually dependent unit.
- After the submissions land: exact replication of coastal and erosion, and pollination regenerated at 2019.
- Then the structural follow-ups and the GEP manuscript numbers regenerated from the verified library.
